newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end modestly higher in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end modestly higher in slow trade.

text.p: Brazilian stocks posted modest gains at the close on Monday in thin turnover as foreign and local activity slowed due to today's U.S. banking holiday, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most active shares rose 0.36 percent or 233 points to 65,829 points. Market turnover was only 198 million reais ($192.3 million), one of the lowest of the year.

Continued concerns over Brazil's swelling trade deficit also affected market trading today, despite remarks by Central Bank chief Gustavo Loyola who once again said October's trade gap, forecast by analysts at $900 million to $1.0 billion, is not worrisome.
Loyola told reporters the trade deficit can be easily financed by foreign direct investment, which he forecasts will reach $9 billion this year.
Between January and September, direct investment in Brazil totaled $5.8 billion.
Bellwether Telebras preferred closed flat at 77.70 reais, while its common stock fell 0.91 percent to close at 65.40 reais.
State mining giant Vale do Rio Doce preferred rose 0.49 percent to 20.45 reais. State oil firm Petrobras rose 2.79 percent, closing at 129 reais.
Power utility Eletrobras preferred rose 1.22 percent to 332 reais.
Analysts said volumes should increase slightly on Tuesday, although investors could remain on the sidelines ahead of the second round of Brazil's municipal elections on Friday.
